Claire’s is currently experiencing an ongoing VPN outage that began on Saturday morning. As a result, file Gateway File  transmission to Appriss Retail has been interrupted. The customer expects regular file delivery to resume once the outage is resolved and has asked whether resumed transmission will be sufficient or if historical/catch-up files will also be required.

Description

Could someone please confirm whether Claire’s will need to provide historical or catch-up files covering the VPN outage period once connectivity is restored?

The customer currently understands that resuming the regular file transmission should be sufficient. However, confirmation is needed on whether:

  • Regular file transmission alone will recover all data missed during the outage.

  • Historical or catch-up files will need to be generated and sent.

  • Any additional recovery or reconciliation steps will be required from the customer.

  • Specific file dates, masks, or delivery details will be needed to validate completeness after transmission resumes.

Once confirmed, Support will communicate the required next steps to the customer.

Note: This customer send the data via API Ingestion: 'c439_rawdata_postransactions'

 

","created":"2026-09-21T17:33:08.510-0400","updated":"2026-09-21T17:33:08.510-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:5c328a05-a6ee-43f9-95be-2b5b0b039ace","displayName":"Sanath Acharya"},"jsdPublic":false},{"id":"3359296","author":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"body":"

1. Environment and scenario

Production. Client 439, Claire's. Ingestion API, endpoint c439_rawdata_postransactions.

  1. Claire's reports a VPN outage on their side since Saturday morning, per the customer email on RTS-207993, Chris Angelica, Director Data Analytics and Integrations.

  2. Gateway file transmission to Appriss has been interrupted since then. No ETA confirmed, customer expects mid week.

  3. Customer asks whether resuming regular transmission recovers all data missed during the outage, or whether historical or catch up files are also required.

Expected: a confirmed answer on whether the ingestion pipeline accepts backdated trading day payloads and whether a trading day already skipped by GNG can be picked up later. Actual: unconfirmed. No Engineering input on file yet for this tenant.

2. Findings

Verified. Client is Claire's, client ID 439, feed c439_rawdata_postransactions. Source: this ticket, comment by Sanath Acharya, 2026-09-21. Verified. Any file whose File Source is Gateway routes to Engineering with product type RTIaaS. Source: internal SLA Rules reference, section 9.5, file monitoring escalation rules. Precedent, not verified on this tenant. RCS-28170, TJX, https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28170 . Same postransactions feed type. Client API keys expired, the feed stopped, one trading day landed at 200408 transactions against a 1700000 minimum, and 23 Work Item definitions were skipped for that day. Once the client fixed the keys and resumed sending, volume recovered on its own with no separate historical file involved. Unverified, from AI triage. Whether the c439_rawdata_postransactions endpoint accepts a payload dated for a past trading day with no window restriction. Unverified, from AI triage. Whether a trading day already closed under the GNG minimum gets reprocessed if a later payload arrives for that same date, or stays permanently skipped for Work Items.

3. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

Claude flagged the RCS-28170 precedent and the GNG mechanism as the likely explanation for what Claire's is asking. I have not run any query or test against this tenant myself yet. This is what the research turned up. Could someone with visibility into the ingestion pipeline evaluate whether it holds for Claire's and share your thoughts?

No conversations held outside this ticket yet.

Support does not have visibility into the ingestion endpoint validation rules or into how the GNG check behaves against late arriving data for an already closed trading day. That is why this is going to Engineering instead of being answered from Support.

4. Still open

  1. Does the c439_rawdata_postransactions endpoint accept a payload dated for a past trading day with no window restriction?

  2. If a trading day already closed under the GNG minimum receives a later payload for that same date, does it get reprocessed for Work Items, or does it stay skipped?

  3. Is Engineering the right owner for this ticket, given the file source is Gateway per SLA Rules 9.5?

Hi @Sanath Acharya , thanks for flagging this. I identified that Claire's ingests via API, endpoint c439_rawdata_postransactions, which is a Gateway file source. Per SLA Rules 9.5 that type routes to Engineering with product type RTIaaS, so I am moving RCS-29037 there instead of answering it from Support.

There is a precedent on file, RCS-28170, TJX, same feed type. The client's API keys expired, the feed stopped, and one trading day landed under the Work Item volume threshold. Once the client resumed sending, that volume recovered on its own with no separate historical file involved. That points to resuming transmission being enough for Claire's too.

One point still needs Engineering to confirm before we can tell the customer for certain. Whether a trading day that fell under the threshold during the outage gets picked up if the missing data arrives late, or stays skipped.

Hello @Juan Martinez,

We received the following communication from Chris Angelica (Chris.Angelica@claires.com) at Claire’s regarding the ongoing integration outage.

Claire’s external integrations have been unavailable since early Saturday, September 19, and their systems remain offline with no confirmed restoration ETA. As a result, data transmissions to Appriss are currently interrupted.

Claire’s will contact us separately to coordinate the recovery once services resume, including:

  • Whether regular file transmissions will resume automatically

  • Whether historical or catch-up files will be provided

  • Whether any additional recovery steps are required

Could the appropriate team please review and advise if there are any specific recovery requirements or considerations that we should communicate to Claire’s?

","created":"2026-09-24T17:01:26.223-0400","updated":"2026-09-24T17:01:26.223-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:71dd07e8-c2b3-41cf-b0a7-ae6f94c5f2de","displayName":"Shreyas Amai"},"jsdPublic":false},{"id":"3363195","author":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"body":"

Hi @Shreyas Amai , thanks for sharing Chris's update.

This widens the scope from what we had on Sep 21. It is no longer a VPN issue only. All of Claire's external integrations have been offline since Saturday Sep 19, with no ETA, so the gap on c439_rawdata_postransactions already covers six trading days and keeps growing.

Chris says he will reach out individually to arrange how data resumes. When he does, could we ask him one thing? Whether their systems are holding the POS transactions from the outage period, and whether they can resend them with the original trading day on each record. That answer decides if resumed transmission alone can cover the gap.

On our side the open question for Engineering stays the same. Whether trading days that stay under the Work Item volume threshold during the outage get picked up once the late data arrives, or stays skipped. I would hold any recovery instructions to Claire's until that is confirmed.

1. Scope update since my Sep 21 note

The outage is wider and longer than first reported. It is no longer a VPN issue only. All of Claire's external integrations have been offline since early Saturday Sep 19, with no restoration ETA.

Item

Sep 21

Sep 24

Cause on Claire's side

VPN outage

All external integrations offline

Start

Saturday morning

Saturday Sep 19, early morning

ETA

Expected mid week

None

Trading days without data

Sep 19 to 21

Sep 19 to 24, six days

2. Environment

Production. Client 439, Claire's. Ingestion API, endpoint c439_rawdata_postransactions. No reproduction steps apply. The feed is silent because the customer cannot send.

3. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

No new testing on this tenant since my Sep 21 note. The precedent and the open points listed there still stand.

Conversations outside this ticket: one customer email. Chris Angelica sent it to all Claire's data partners on Sep 24 at 10:44 ET, and Shreyas Amai attached it to this ticket the same day. Chris says he will contact each partner individually to agree on three points. Whether transmission simply turns back on, whether historical updates are needed, and any other topic.

Support has no visibility into how the ingestion endpoint validates backdated payloads or how the GNG check treats late data for a trading day already closed.

4. Still open

  1. Does c439_rawdata_postransactions accept payloads dated for a past trading day, and is there a maximum lookback window? The gap is already six trading days and has no end date yet.

  2. When late data arrives for a trading day that closed under the GNG minimum, does that day get reprocessed for Work Items, or does it stay skipped?

  3. If those days stay skipped, is there a supported way to trigger Work Item generation for them once the data is complete?

  4. What should Support ask Claire's to send when Chris reaches out, so the recovery can be validated as complete?
